# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Daily Update (Feb 2, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
The day saw a new design document proposed for migrating to SuperDisputeGame. Discussions continued on issues related to `op-supernode`'s safe label adjusting, Flashblocks support in Geth, and `BlockNotFoundError` in the ETH bridge tutorial.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

No new features, bug fixes, code refactoring, documentation enhancements, or tests were added.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
A new pull request, [#365](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/365), was opened to introduce a design document for migrating to SuperDisputeGame.

## CLOSED ISSUES
No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were opened today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### `op-supernode`: Safe Label Adjusting Discussion
Discussion on [#18976](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/18976) continued with `geoknee` providing an update after further consideration. The updated perspective leans towards the Consensus Layer (CL) maintaining the full set of pointers (Unsafe, Safe, Canonical, Finalized) and remaining the sole controller of the execution engine (EL). This approach suggests that the `op-supernode` should control the engine via the virtual node/CL in normal operation. This has the benefit of allowing virtual nodes to return rich sync status and aligns with the idea of an "authority" object within the virtual node.

### Flashblocks Support in Geth
The discussion on [#756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/756) saw `maoueh` provide a link to their `op-geth` version which includes Firehose Live Tracer and Flashblock(s) support. This follows `sunjiahui`'s comment on February 1st, expressing interest in merging this functionality into `op-geth` due to the disk space and operational complexity of running archive versions of Reth.

### `BlockNotFoundError` in ETH Bridge Tutorial
On [#1956](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/1956), `opfocus` highlighted a potential lack of output root validation in Viem's `Withdrawals guide` and related actions, contrasting it with the validation step present in Optimism SDK packages. This comment builds on previous discussions about a "contamination" issue affecting tutorial examples on Sepolia, where `waitToProve` is executed before the corresponding state root is published to L1, leading to incorrect output. A temporary workaround involving manual retrieval and override of output data was previously suggested.
